virals.hook: Delegating UI/UX design straight to a code abstraction is a big mistake. That's exactly why we're seeing so mu
virals.text:
Delegating UI/UX design straight to a code abstraction is a big mistake. That's exactly why we're seeing so much slop, even though there are models with taste like Opus 5.5, Fable 5.2 and Gemini 4

When building design with code, models spend a lot of context and compute on things that have nothing to do with design. As a result, you have to burn a lot of time and tokens on endless iterations just to get a barely acceptable result

Neither Claude Design, nor Pencil, nor Open Design, nor Figma has managed to become a good industry standard for building UI/UX in the era of AI agents

This problem has yet to be solved. We need to come up with a different, better-suited abstraction for this task. And it's definitely not code

Fix the oversharing first. Then invite the agents.

drafts.text:
"Not activated. Yet." got more replies asking how than any post I've done this week.

So here's the short version of Autopilot readiness:

- pick a small pilot group, not the whole tenant
- check what data they can already reach
- decide who owns the agent when it gets something wrong
- write down what success looks like before day one

Turning it on is the easy part.
